headline: FO briefing Fri Oct 23) -- Pakistan and Saudi Arabia complete Makkah Joint Defence Agreement ratification
dek: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (signed Aug 7 in Mecca by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye); Turkiye is still completing its domestic procedures after submitting the pact to parliament earlier in the week (Turkish parliament notice…
sources: Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan, weekly media briefing, Islamabad
fault_line: A real deterrent shield for Riyadh under Ansar Allah fire -- or a paper pact that still needs a collective vote before a single soldier moves?

sections.what_happened: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (signed Aug 7 in Mecca by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye); Turkiye is still completing its domestic procedures after submitting the pact to parliament earlier in the week (Turkish parliament notice dated Oct 20). Article 2 treats an external armed attack on any party as an attack on all, with the nature and extent of assistance decided collectively. The FO says ratification and operationalisation remain under discussion, including in the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, which last met Oct 5 and called for immediate implementation and rapid deployment of agreed forces to Saudi Arabia, subject to national legislation. The FO endorsed the 16-article text released via the Turkish parliament and said there are no hidden provisions. Context: the announcement came as Saudi Arabia faces Ansar Allah missile attacks (Taif/Yanbu intercepts recorded 1500-01).
sections.what_verified: Pakistan FO statement (primary source) carried by Dawn, Arab News, Business Recorder and Dunya News; FO transcript quoted consistently across carries. Earlier single-blog pact claim (0800-07) is superseded for ratification only -- no deployment has been announced.
sections.what_disputed: Turkiye has NOT ratified, so the pact is not fully in force for all three signatories; the FO itself says ratification and operationalisation remain under discussion; no troop deployment has been announced, and any assistance is subject to collective decision and national legislation. The FO says the pact is defensive, consistent with UN Charter Article 51, and not directed against any particular country.
sections.why_matters: The August pact just became real for two of its three members -- while Saudi Arabia is under missile attack. What 'attack on one is attack on all' actually triggers: nothing automatic.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (big-missed; FO briefing Fri Oct 23) -- Pakistan and Saudi Arabia complete Makkah Joint Defence Agreement ratification; Turkiye still pending

totw_analysis: Our read: The August pact just became real for two of its three members -- while Saudi Arabia is under missile attack. What 'attack on one is attack on all' actually triggers: nothing automatic. The fault line our audience is arguing over: A real deterrent shield for Riyadh under Ansar Allah fire -- or a paper pact that still needs a collective vote before a single soldier moves?
